books.name: Isaiah
gists: Judah is called to repent from rebellion and injustice for restoration.
The LORD's house draws nations for learning and peace in the last days.
The LORD removes support, leading to oppression and desolation in Jerusalem.
Seven women seek one man; God preserves Zion's remnant.
God condemns Israel's unfruitfulness, promising judgment for injustice and greed.
Isaiah sees God’s holiness, is cleansed, and commissioned to prophesy.
Isaiah assures Ahaz of God's protection against warring nations and promises Immanuel.
Isaiah names his son as a sign of impending Assyrian judgment.
A child named Wonderful Counselor brings hope to Israel despite impending judgment.
God condemns oppression, using Assyria but promising eventual deliverance for Israel.
A righteous ruler from Jesse unites and brings peace to Israel.
The speaker praises God for salvation and encourages joyful proclamation.
Isaiah prophesies Babylon's destruction by Medes as divine judgment.
God promises Israel's restoration and condemns Babylon's pride and oppression.
Moab mourns its desolation and fleeing people amidst widespread devastation.
Moab faces destruction, urging for justice amid pride and desolation.
Damascus will be ruined, and Jacob's glory will fade.
Ethiopia's land will face impending judgment and tribute to Zion.
Egypt faces judgment and confusion, yet will ultimately seek God.
Isaiah symbolically reveals Egypt and Ethiopia's impending shame under Assyria.
Isaiah prophesies Babylon's fall and judgments on Elam, Media, Dumah, and Kedar.
Jerusalem's leaders fail amid crisis, while God judges prideful Shebna.
Tyre faces destruction and desolation but will eventually be restored.
The LORD devastates the earth for sin, causing mourning and humility.
The Lord promises refuge, a feast, and the destruction of Moab.
Judah praises God's protection and promises resurrection for the righteous.
God slays Leviathan, protects Israel, and gathers His people to worship.
Judgment on Ephraim's prideful leaders while God promises hope for the faithful.
God will restore Jacob despite the people's spiritual blindness and enemies.
Judah seeks Egypt's help, rejecting God, leading to shame and judgment.
Trusting Egypt over the LORD leads to disaster; repentance is urged.
A righteous king brings peace and assurance after judgment.
Judgment on the treacherous; Zion becomes a secure refuge for the righteous.
The LORD's wrath brings desolation to Idumea and its land.
The wilderness blossoms as God brings salvation and healing.
Sennacherib's messenger mocks Hezekiah's trust in God and Egypt.
Hezekiah seeks Isaiah; God defends Jerusalem, defeating Assyria.
Hezekiah prays, receives healing, and celebrates with a psalm of thanks.
Hezekiah shows treasures to envoys; Isaiah predicts Babylon’s conquest.
God announces comfort, preparation for His coming, and strength renewal.
God assures Israel of strength, challenges idols, and promises provision.
God's servant brings justice, guides the blind, and calls for praise.
The LORD promises redemption, renewal, and forgiveness for unfaithful Israel.
The LORD affirms Israel's chosen status and condemns idolatry.
God anoints Cyrus, asserting His sovereignty and offering salvation to Israel.
Idols are powerless; the LORD promises care and salvation for Israel.
Babylon's pride is shattered, leading to her sudden ruin and desolation.
God rebukes Israel, declares sovereignty, and promises redemption and peace.
God promises His servant will restore Israel and be a light.
The obedient servant trusts God despite shame, urging faith amid darkness.
God comforts Zion, promising salvation, restoration, and protection.
Zion is called to rejoice, proclaiming peace and salvation from captivity.
The suffering servant bears sins, bringing healing and justification to many.
The Lord promises the barren woman abundant offspring and everlasting protection.
The LORD invites all to seek Him for life and restoration.
God promises salvation to the faithful and condemns selfish leaders.
The righteous find peace, while the wicked face rejection and warning.
God calls for genuine fasting that supports the oppressed and honors justice.
Sin separates people from God, but the Redeemer will bring salvation.
Zion becomes a glorified city attracting nations and eternal joy.
God anoints to bring salvation, comfort, and restoration to His people.
The LORD guarantees Jerusalem's salvation and renames her, ensuring protection.
God's vengeance and mercy are proclaimed amid Israel's rebellion and lament.
The people plea for mercy, confessing sins and seeking restoration.
God condemns rebellion but promises blessings to a faithful remnant.
God promises comfort, judgment, and a new creation for all nations.

anchors.text: Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me.
Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.

For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.
Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.
But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.

When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.
Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth: for I am God, and there is none else.
But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.
For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD.

The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound;
But we are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags; and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, have taken us away.
For all those things hath mine hand made, and all those things have been, saith the LORD: but to this man will I look, even to him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembleth at my word.

books.name: Jeremiah
gists: Jeremiah is appointed by God to prophesy despite expected opposition.
God laments Israel's idolatry and warns of impending judgment.
Israel's unfaithfulness is met with God's call to repentance and restoration.
Israel is urged to repent to avoid northern invasion and destruction.
God warns Jerusalem of impending judgment due to persistent unfaithfulness.
Jeremiah warns of Jerusalem's impending destruction and calls for mourning.
Jeremiah warns Judah of judgment for false worship and injustice.
Judah faces destruction for idolatry and ignoring God's judgment.
Jeremiah mourns Israel's sin and announces God's coming judgment and exile.
God warns Israel about idol worship and impending judgment.
Jeremiah warns Judah of covenant curses and faces plots against him.
Jeremiah laments the wicked's prosperity; God promises judgment and restoration.
Jeremiah's ruined girdle symbolizes Judah's pride and impending judgment.
Judah experiences drought; Jeremiah pleads for mercy amid impending judgment.
God decrees judgment for sin while promising restoration for the faithful.
Jeremiah is commanded to remain unmarried and proclaim impending judgment and restoration.
Judah’s sin results in exile; trust in God is rewarded.
God warns Israel and Judah to repent or face judgment.
Jeremiah breaks a pot to signify Jerusalem's impending judgment and destruction.
Jeremiah endures persecution but remains committed to proclaiming God's message.
Jeremiah warns Zedekiah of Babylon’s siege and the need for justice.
God demands justice, warning unrighteous kings of impending exile and desolation.
God condemns false shepherds and promises a righteous leader.
Jeremiah uses figs to symbolize Judah's faithful exiles and rebels' destruction.
Jeremiah foretells judgment and destruction for disobedient nations.
Jeremiah warns Judah in the temple, facing accusations but ultimately spared.
Jeremiah urges submission to Babylon and condemns false prophets.
Hananiah falsely prophesies deliverance; Jeremiah declares him a false prophet.
Jeremiah advises exiles in Babylon to seek peace and warns against false prophets.
God promises restoration and healing for Israel and Judah.
God promises Israel's restoration, a new covenant, and everlasting love.
Jeremiah buys a field amid Jerusalem's impending fall, symbolizing hope.
God promises restoration, healing, and a righteous leader for Jerusalem.
Zedekiah is warned of Jerusalem's fall and consequences of breaking God's law.
Rechabites’ obedience contrasts Judah’s disobedience, securing Jonadab’s legacy.
Jeremiah's scroll is burned by Jehoiakim, prompting a new scroll's creation.
Jeremiah is imprisoned for warning of Jerusalem's impending fall.
Jeremiah is imprisoned but later rescued, advising surrender for survival.
Jerusalem falls; Zedekiah is captured, blinded, and Jeremiah is spared.
Jeremiah stays in Judah with Gedaliah despite warnings of a plot.
Ishmael kills Gedaliah and others, then flees with captives.
The people seek God’s guidance; disobedience leads to disaster.
Jeremiah warns against fleeing to Egypt, but the remnant defies God.
Jews in Egypt reject Jeremiah's warnings and continue idolatry, facing judgment.
Jeremiah reassures Baruch, urging humility amid impending judgment and adversity.
Jeremiah prophesies Egypt's defeat and Israel's future restoration.
God pronounces judgment on the Philistines, predicting destruction and desolation.
The LORD condemns Moab for pride, foretelling desolation and eventual restoration.
God judges several nations for pride and violence, promising future restoration.
Babylon will be destroyed for pride, while Israel and Judah will return.
God will destroy Babylon and its inhabitants will flee.
Jerusalem falls to Babylon; Zedekiah is captured, and captives are exiled.

anchors.text: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.
The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?
For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.

But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel; After those days, saith the LORD, I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people.
Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not.

books.name: Lamentations
gists: Jerusalem mourns desolation and suffering from sin and divine wrath.
The LORD's anger destroys Jerusalem, leaving its people in despair.
The speaker endures suffering but hopes in God's mercy and justice.
Zion’s former glory is destroyed by famine, despair, and divine wrath.
The people mourn their suffering and plead for God's restoration.

anchors.text: It is of the LORD’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.

books.name: Ezekiel
gists: Ezekiel sees a vision of God’s glory with living creatures and wheels.
Ezekiel is called to speak God's words to rebellious Israel.
Ezekiel eats a scroll and is appointed watchman to Israel.
Ezekiel symbolizes Jerusalem's siege and impending judgment through enacted prophecies.
Ezekiel symbolizes Jerusalem's imminent destruction and consequences for defying God.
Ezekiel prophesies judgment on Israel’s altars and idols, with a remnant remaining.
God announces impending judgment and destruction upon Israel for their sins.
Ezekiel witnesses idol worship in Jerusalem, provoking God's anger and judgment.
God's judgment begins in Jerusalem, marking the faithful and slaying the unmarked.
God's glory departs from the temple, moving above the cherubim.
Wickedness leads to judgment, but God promises restoration for Israel.
Ezekiel symbolizes imminent exile and God's swift judgment on Israel.
God condemns false prophets for spreading lies and false peace.
Elders face judgment for idolatry; a remnant will endure.
Jerusalem is compared to a worthless vine destined for destruction.
Jerusalem, nurtured by God, turns to idolatry and faces judgment.
Ezekiel depicts a riddle about Babylon's captivity and God's future restoration.
Each soul bears its own sin; repentance leads to life.
A lioness laments her fallen cubs and lost power.
God recounts Israel's rebellion, condemns idolatry, yet promises restoration.
Ezekiel prophesies judgment as Babylon prepares to strike Jerusalem.
Ezekiel condemns Jerusalem for corruption and impending divine judgment.
Aholah and Aholibah's idolatry leads to God's judgment and destruction.
Ezekiel symbolizes Jerusalem's destruction and mourns his wife's death silently.
Ezekiel prophesies judgment against nations rejoicing over Israel's suffering.
Tyre boasts over Jerusalem's fall, but God decrees its destruction.
Ezekiel mourns Tyre's impending downfall and loss of prosperity.
God condemns the prideful prince and king of Tyre, promising restoration for Israel.
Ezekiel prophesies Egypt's desolation, exile, and eventual restoration.
Judgment is pronounced on Egypt; Nebuchadnezzar will devastate the land.
God compares Pharaoh to a mighty tree destined to fall.
Ezekiel laments Pharaoh's downfall, symbolizing Egypt's impending destruction.
Ezekiel is appointed watchman, warning Israel of impending judgment and repentance.
God condemns neglectful leaders and promises to restore His flock.
Ezekiel prophesies Mount Seir's destruction for its hatred toward Israel.
The Lord promises Israel's restoration, cleansing, and a new heart.
Ezekiel prophesies to dry bones, symbolizing Israel's restoration and unity.
Gog invades Israel, but God will thwart him with judgment.

Ezekiel sees a vision of a rebuilt temple with detailed measurements.
Ezekiel describes the temple's dimensions and intricate design features.
Ezekiel sees the priests' chambers for offerings and garment changes.
God's glory enters the temple, establishing His dwelling among Israel.
The east gate is shut; God's glory fills the temple.
God instructs a fair division of land and offerings for worship.
The east gate opens for worship on Sabbaths and new moons.
Waters from the temple revive life, restoring land and boundaries for Israel.
Israel's land is divided among tribes, with a sacred city for God.

anchors.text: Say unto them, As I live, saith the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live: turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways; for why will ye die, O house of Israel?
A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.
Thus saith the Lord GOD unto these bones; Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you, and ye shall live:

books.name: Daniel
gists: Daniel and friends honor God, gaining wisdom by refusing the king's food.
Nebuchadnezzar's dream reveals kingdoms; Daniel interprets it, showcasing God's sovereignty.
Three men refuse to worship a golden image and survive the furnace.
Nebuchadnezzar's pride leads to his humiliation until he honors God.
Belshazzar's feast leads to God's judgment and his subsequent death.
Daniel is saved from lions for praying, leading the king to honor God.
Daniel dreams of four beasts representing kingdoms, culminating in divine judgment.
Daniel's vision reveals future kingdoms and a persecuting king.
Daniel confesses Israel’s sins and receives a prophetic revelation.
Daniel mourns, sees a glorious vision, and learns of spiritual conflict.
Kings conflict, a vile ruler defiles the sanctuary and faces ruin.
Michael defends Israel; the dead rise, and Daniel seals the book.

anchors.text: And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.
If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king.

Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.
And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.
